title: Prepare unshelled groundnut sample for grading

lessons.title: Setting up and checking the sample
lessons.html:
Setting up and checking the sample

An unshelled groundnut sample has the nuts still in their pods (shells). Before the grader can grade it, the sample must be prepared: weighed, cleaned of foreign matter, shelled and sorted into parts. Your job is to prepare it carefully so the grader gets a true result. A mistake here changes what the farmer is paid.

Prepare the work area

  • Clean the bench, trays, scale, sieves and sheller. Old nuts or shells from the last sample will spoil the next result.
  • Check that the scale is working and set to zero. Use the check weight if your depot has one.
  • Have trays or containers ready for each part, each with a label.
  • Wear a dust mask and wash your hands first.

Check the sample

  1. Check that the label and seal are whole and the sample matches the delivery ticket.
  2. Write the sample details on the grading worksheet.
  3. Divide the sample with the sample divider to the size your procedure needs. Do not scoop.

Remove foreign matter

Foreign matter is anything that is not a groundnut pod or kernel: sand, soil, stones, sticks, leaves, plant stems, glass, plastic, and other seeds.

  1. Weigh the working sample and write the mass down.
  2. Sieve it with the sieve your procedure uses to remove sand and soil.
  3. Pick out stones, sticks and other foreign matter by hand.
  4. Weigh all the foreign matter together and write the mass down.

Look out for poisonous seeds such as thorn apple (stinkblaar) and for glass or metal. Put them aside and show the grader. They can affect the grade or cause a delivery to be rejected.

lessons.title: Shelling, sorting and handing over
lessons.html:
Shelling and sorting

Shelling the sample

  1. Weigh the clean pods.
  2. Shell them with the sample sheller, or by hand if your depot does it that way.
  3. Do not crush the kernels. Damaged kernels from rough shelling give a wrong grade.
  4. Catch everything: kernels, shells and loose skins.

Sorting the parts

Separate the shelled sample into the parts your grading worksheet asks for, for example:

  • Whole sound kernels.
  • Split and broken kernels.
  • Damaged kernels: mouldy, insect damaged, discoloured, shrivelled.
  • Shells (hulls).

Weigh each part and write the mass on the worksheet. The grader uses these masses to work out percentages and the grade. Check that the parts add up close to the mass of the clean pods. A big difference means something was lost or a weighing mistake was made. Check again before handing over.

Mouldy kernels

Kernels with grey, green or yellow-green mould may carry aflatoxin. Keep them separate. Do not smell them closely or blow dust off them. Show them to the grader.

Handing over

  • Give the trays and the worksheet to the grader together.
  • Keep the parts in labelled trays until the grader is finished.
  • Store the retained part of the sample as your procedure says.

Safety and hygiene

  • Keep fingers out of the sheller. Switch it off before you clear it.
  • Wear a dust mask.
  • Do not eat nuts from samples.
  • Clean the bench and tools before the next sample.

Key points

  • Clean all equipment and zero the scale before each sample.
  • Remove and weigh foreign matter, and show poisonous seeds to the grader.
  • Shell gently and catch everything.
  • Sort into kernels, broken, damaged and shells and weigh each part.
  • Check that the masses add up before handing over.
